For each year during the Track Record Period, the majority of our revenue was derived from
our five largest customers through the sales of ethanol. There is a concentration in our customer
base, because our ethanol is primarily used as automotive fuel and our major customers are leading
domestic oil and gas producers. Given their strong demand for sustainable energy solutions like
ethanolandtheirpresenceinthemarket,wehaveshapedourstrategytoprimarilyengagewiththese
key players. According to Frost & Sullivan, such customer concentration is common in the
industrial gas and energy sectors due to the scale of operations and investment required.While this
focus allows us to establish deep partnerships with our major clients, we recognize the potential
risks of reliance on a limited customer base. Please refer to “Risk Factors — Risks Relating to Our
Business and Industry — A significant portion of our revenue was derived from a concentrated
customer base during the Track Record Period.” To mitigate the risks associated with customer
concentration, we are actively exploring opportunities in emerging markets and diversifying our
customer base. In addition, we aim to create a balanced revenue stream by offering our low-carbon
integrated solutions to industrial clients who are seeking to implement our proprietary synthetic
biotechnology in their facilities.
For each year during the Track Record Period, none of our five largest customers were also
our suppliers. During the Track Record Period, none of our Directors, Supervisors, their respective
associatesoranyofourShareholders(whoownedor,totheknowledgeofourDirectors,hadowned
more than 5% of our Shares) had any interest in any of our five largest customers for each year
during the Track Record Period. During the Track Record Period and as of the Latest Practicable
Date, we did not have any material disputes with our customers.

SUPPLIERS
DuringtheTrackRecordPeriod,weprimarilyuseddomesticsupplierstoprocureawiderange
of goods and services including raw materials, utilities and energy, auxiliary materials and other
facilitating goods and services.
We have established systems and procedures for supplier selection, tendering, procurement
planning,contractmanagement,andrawmaterialinspectionandacceptance.Suppliersarecarefully
selected based on a set of evaluation and assessment criteria, including production capacity,
delivery reliability, qualifications with relevant licenses or permits, payment terms and price
competitiveness. These processes ensure a stable and reliable supply of materials for our
production. We determine different pricing mechanisms depending on the nature of materials
required in our production. We also closely monitor the quality of all materials provided by our
suppliers to ensure compliance with our stringent requirements. During the Track Record Period,
except for the relevant litigations with Jiyuan Junyi which were fully settled and withdrawn, we
maintained stable relationships with our major suppliers and did not experience any material
disputes.
Raw Materials
Our primary raw material is carbon-containing industrial off-gas, which is directly sourced
through pipelines from upstream steel and ferroalloy mills in the PRC. These gas pipelines are
integral to our production process. Since our production relies on carbon-containing industrial
off-gas, most of our carbon-containing industrial off-gas suppliers were our connected persons
during the Track Record Period.
We entered into long-term procurement agreements with our carbon-containing industrial
off-gas suppliers of steel and ferroalloy mills for all our production facilities. Our Directors
confirmedthattherewasnomaterialbreachofthetermsofsuchlong-termprocurementagreements
during the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date.
Below is a summary of the material terms of typical procurement agreements that we entered
into with our carbon-containing industrial off-gas suppliers during the Track Record Period:
Specification  The agreements specify the types of carbon-containing
industrial off-gas to be supplied.
Duration  ForourHebeiShoulangPhaseIproductionfacility,theinitial
term is ten years, which is subject to renewal upon mutual
agreement between the parties.
For our Shoulang Jiyuan, Ningxia Binze and Guizhou Jinze
production facilities, the terms of the agreements are tied to
the respective duration of our subsidiaries Shoulang Jiyuan,
Ningxia Binze and Guizhou Jinze, which are all set at 20
years from their respective dates of establishment under their
articles of associations.
Price  The prices are calculated based on the basic electricity price
or coal price, combined with the calorific value of industrial
off-gas which is primarily determined by the carbon
monoxide concentration. The energy content of the industrial
off-gas, particularly the carbon monoxide levels, is related to
energy prices, as both electricity and coal prices reflect the
energy value in the same way.
The prices will be adjusted at least once every two years to
ensure they remain aligned with electricity and coal prices,
and reflect changes in the actual quality of the supplied gas,
such as variations in carbon monoxide concentration.

The purchased volume of industrial off-gas at Hebei Shoulang Phase I production facility
decreased in the Track Record Period, primarily due to a decline in the carbon monoxide (CO)
concentration in the supplied industrial off-gas and an increase in impurities harmful to microbial
strains in 2025. Firstly, lower CO concentration reduced the effective carbon content of the
feedstock,andbecauseCOmustdissolveintothefermentationbrothbeforebeingmetabolized,less
CO could be dissolved per unit volume, and this limitation cannot be offset simply by increasing
off-gas flow. As a result, microbial strains were able to process and consume a smaller volume of
industrial off-gas. Secondly, impurities harmful to microbial strains in the industrial off-gas
increased in 2025 due to the upstream supplier’s internal production adjustments. These harmful
impurities disrupted stable strain proliferation, reduced the strains’ ability to process CO, and
increased the frequency of re-inoculation. As a result, microbial strains consumed less industrial
– 143 –

=== PAGE 153 ===
BUSINESS
off-gas and experienced further declines in CO-processing efficiency, leading to additional
reductions in production. To mitigate the adverse impact of these harmful impurities on the
microbial strains, we reduced the intake of industrial off-gas containing such impurities, which in
turn resulted in Hebei Shoulang purchasing a lower volume of industrial off-gas during the Track
Record Period.
The average purchase price of industrial off-gas at the Hebei Shoulang Phase I production
facility fluctuated during the Track Record Period as changes in CO concentration caused
corresponding changes in calorific value, which is the basis for pricing—lower calorific value
resulting in lower purchase prices. Hebei Shoulang purchased industrial off-gas at adjusted prices
in accordance with the agreement, whereas no such price adjustments were required for our other
three production facilities, as their off-gas feedstock did not experience significant declines in CO
concentration. The average CO concentrations and adjusted prices for Hebei Shoulang Phase I for

The purchase volume of industrial off-gas at Ningxia Binze production facility from both

Shoulang Jiyuan production facility
The maximum industrial off-gas volume required for reaching the full design capacity of
Shoulang Jiyuan production facility is approximately 300 million Nm3/year. Shoulang Jiyuan
purchases industrial off-gas directly from Jiyuan Metallurgical, and the industrial off-gas provided
to Shoulang Jiyuan by Jiyuan Metallurgical is generated from its own operations as well as
purchased from another nearby ferroalloy plant. The total maximum industrial off-gas can be
producedbythesetwoplantsis450millionNm3/year,whichisgreaterthanthemaximumindustrial
off-gas volume required for reaching the full design capacity of the Shoulang Jiyuan production
facility. In addition, Shoulang Jiyuan regularly communicates with upstream industrial off-gas
suppliers to align on gas supply and maintenance plans, so as to maintain and overhaul production
facility at the same time as the upstream.
Jiyuan Metallurgical is an enterprise focuses on the production and processing of ferrous and
non-ferrous metal alloys founded in 2003. Headquartered in Pingluo County, Ningxia, Jiyuan
Metallurgical has a registered capital of RMB299 million and employs over 600 employees.As of
the Latest Practicable Date, Jiyuan Metallurgical was supplying industrial off-gas based on the
existing contractual obligations with us, and the local government was planning to establish a
unified off-gas company to collect industrial off-gas generated by enterprises in the industrial park,
and uniformly construct transmission pipelines and supporting facilities. This unified off-gas
company is expected to collect off-gas from nearby ferroalloy companies, act as a supplementary
gas source for Shoulang Jiyuan and, when necessary, uniformly provide industrial off-gas to
Shoulang Jiyuan (and Ningxia Binze) upon completion, which is expected to be able to satisfy the
gas supply needs for Shoulang Jiyuan and Ningxia Binze after it commences operation (should this
be required), thus minimizing any future negative impact caused by supply disruptions with the
existing industrial off-gas suppliers of Shoulang Jiyuan and Ningxia Binze. It is currently expected
to be able to commence supply industrial off-gas in the first quarter of 2027.

Guizhou Jinze production facility
The maximum industrial off-gas volume required for reaching the full design capacity of
Guizhou Jinze production facility is approximately 450 million Nm3/year. Guizhou Jinze directly
purchases industrial off-gas from Yuqian Manganese, whose maximum industrial off-gas supply is
480millionNm3/year,whichisgreaterthanthemaximumindustrialoff-gasvolumerequiredforthe

communicates with upstream industrial off-gas suppliers to align on gas supply and maintenance
plans, so as to maintain and overhaul the production facilities at the same time as the upstream.
Jinyuan Suiyang, the predecessor ofYuqian Manganese, underwent equity restructuring in the
first quarter of 2025 and its gas supply was suspended during this period. During the equity
restructuring period, production suspension was necessary to: (i) facilitate a comprehensive
inspection on the inventory and assets of such companies, and (ii) enable the original and the new
owner of such companies to conduct inspection on the production equipment to identify potential
production and safety issues, and to perform equipment maintenance and repair.According to Frost
& Sullivan, suspension of production during the equity restructuring of an industrial enterprise is
a common practice in the industry. Yuqian Manganese also conducted safety inspections and
comprehensive maintenance and repair for its production facility and Guizhou Jinze production
facilityalsocompleteditsannualmaintenanceduringthisperiod.WhenYuqianManganeseresumed
production in April 2025, the gas supply volume had been low due to unstable production during
its commissioning phase; however, after carrying out multiple technical transformations, normal
production and industrial off-gas supply was restored by the start of December 2025.
There are no potential alternative industrial off-gas supplier which is in the proximity of
Guizhou Jinze production facility.
Due to the nature of our business, where we rely on major suppliers for carbon-containing
industrial off-gas, our suppliers are notably concentrated and most of them are our connected
persons.While this concentration provides stability in terms of reliable sourcing, it also exposes us
tosupplychainriskssuchasinsufficientsupplyofindustrialoff-gasduetosuspensionofoperations
by upstream suppliers, declining industrial off-gas quality, and price fluctuations of industrial
off-gas, and reliance on a limited number of suppliers. Please refer to “Risk Factors — Risks
Relating to Our Business and Industry — We have a concentrated supplier base and any increase
in the prices of their products could materially and adversely affect our business, financial
condition, results of operations and profitability” and “— Our business may be materially and
adversely affected if there is any significant downtime at the production facilities of ourselves and
our suppliers, which prevents us from achieving sufficient utilization of our production facilities”
for further details.
Besides the abovementioned measures we took including arrangement with potential
alternative suppliers and the unified government-led off-gas company, we focus on strengthening
relationships with our existing suppliers by signing long-term procurement agreements, among
others. Moreover, according to Frost & Sullivan, the sale prices of silicon manganese alloy is
expected to gradually recover. Please refer to “Industry Overview — Overview of the Steel and
Ferroalloy Industry — Analysis of China’s Steel and Ferroalloy Comprehensive Price Index” for
further details.As a result, we believe that disruptions to our upstream suppliers due to unfavorable
market conditions in the coming years will be less likely to to occur, thus minimizing the potential
impact on our production.
Based on the above, our Directors are of the view that the risks associated with our reliance
on a limited number of carbon-containing industrial off-gas suppliers and potential supply chain
disruptions will not have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition or results
of operations. Having considered the views of our Directors above and based on the due diligence

INVENTORY MANAGEMENT
Our inventory consists primarily of auxiliary materials for our production and our finished
products. We manage our inventory levels in real-time to ensure optimal stock levels to support
production and delivery schedules. During the Track Record Period, we did not identify any

BUSINESS SUSTAINABILITY
Overview
Faced with the threat of increasing global greenhouse gas emissions and climate change,
major economies around the world have formulated carbon reduction policies in response.
Leveraging the growth opportunities in CCUS industry, we expanded our production facilities
during the Track Record Period, despite our historical losses since our establishment. However,
during the Track Record Period, our revenue decreased by 4.9% from RMB592.6 million in 2023
to RMB563.6 million in 2024 primarily as a result of (i) maintenance conducted by our upstream
suppliers of industrial off-gases, which led to a reduction in our sales volume of our ethanol and
microbial protein products in 2024 and (ii) a decrease of 15.6% in the average selling price of
ethanol in 2024 as compared with that of 2023. Our revenue further decreased by 7.4% from
RMB563.6 million in 2024 to RMB521.7 million in 2025. Such decrease was primarily driven by
the combining factors including the low average selling price of ethanol, the fluctuation of our
production volume and the fact that our low-carbon integrated solutions did not generate any
revenue in 2025, as further detailed below.
Our Performance during the Track Record Period
During the Track Record Period, we incurred a cumulative net loss of approximately
RMB680.6 million, primarily due to the following reasons: (i) we invested in R&D and incurred an
accumulative R&D expense of RMB120.4 million during theTrack Record Period; (ii) we incurred
depreciation and amortization costs from our established production facilities; (iii) the CO
concentration in the gas supplied by the upstream industrial off-gas suppliers of Hebei Shoulang
Phase I production facility gradually decreased and the impurities harmful to microbial strains in
the upstream industrial off-gas increased, resulting in low capacity utilization rate and operational
lossesofthefacility;(iv)theinsufficientgassupplyfromindustrialoff-gassupplierswhichresulted
in low capacity utilization of our production facilities of Shoulang Jiyuan, Ningxia Binze and
Guizhou Jinze, led to operational losses; and (v) while fuel ethanol prices remained stable in 2023
and the first half of 2024, they experienced a sharp decline in the second half of 2024 to 2025 due
to a large amount of low-cost coal-based ethanol entering into the fuel ethanol market as well as
the subsequent “involution-style” competition as further detailed below, which significantly and
negatively affected our revenue for 2024 and 2025.
In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our overall production volume of ethanol amounted to 86,564 tons,
88,396tonsand88,339tons,respectively.Thesimilarbutslightlyloweroverallproductionvolume
of ethanol in 2025 as compared to 2024 was mainly attributed to the reduced production at Hebei
Shoulang and the operational halt at Guizhou Jinze for reasons discussed below, which negatively
impacted our overall performance.With the resumption of normal production of Guizhou Jinze and
the increase in production volume of Hebei Shoulang as further discussed below, we have recorded
28,758 tons of ethanol production in the first quarter of 2026, representing an increase of 30.2% as
compared to the quarterly average in 2025.
Our average selling price of ethanol in 2025 amounted to RMB4,641 per ton, which remained
at a similar level as compared to the fourth quarter in 2024, but was RMB428 per ton lower as
compared to the annual average selling price of ethanol in 2024, reflecting that the average selling
price in 2025 did not recover to the similar level in 2024. The reason of the further deteriorated
average selling price of ethanol in 2025 was because of the “involution-style” competition
following the prohibition of the lower-priced coal-based ethanol from entering into the fuel ethanol
market. Please refer to “— Path to Profitability” for further explanation of such development in
2025. The average selling price of fuel ethanol has increased in the first quarter of 2026 as
compared to 2025, which is expected to remain at a comparable level throughout the year and, if
so, benefit our average selling price of our ethanol products. Please refer to “— Business
Sustainability — Quarterly Trend of Fuel Ethanol Prices in China and Correlation with our
Profitability” and “Summary — Recent Development and No Material Adverse Change.”
Particularly, for a standalone analysis of the reasons of further deterioration of our
performance in 2025 as compared to 2024, please see “— Reasons for the Deterioration in Our
Financial Performance in 2025 as Compared to 2024” below.

Revenue and Average Selling Price of Ethanol
Our revenue was RMB592.6 million, RMB563.6 million and RMB521.7 million for the years

The decrease in revenue from 2023 to 2024 was primarily due to: (i) insufficient upstream
industry off-gas supply due to market conditions in the ferroalloy industry leading to lower-than-

large-scale coal-based ethanol projects commenced operations in 2024 with low production costs.
The rapid capacity expansion in coal-based ethanol severely disrupted the price of ethanol in the
fuel ethanol market in 2024.

Gross Profit/Loss
Our gross profit was RMB17.7 million, gross loss was RMB93.3 million and gross loss was
RMB127.7 million for the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively.
Our decrease from gross profit in 2023 to gross loss in 2024 was primarily due to: (i)
lower-than-expected production output in the first half of 2024; (ii) the declining average ethanol
selling prices in 2024 as discussed in the reasons for fluctuations in revenue above, which led to
a material drop of our revenue; and (iii) increased depreciation and amortization costs (as part of
the costs of sales) from RMB88.4 million in 2023 to RMB113.9 million in 2024. Taking into
consideration of the analysis of revenue fluctuations above, a gross loss was incurred in 2024 as a

In 2025, our gross loss widened by RMB34.3 million as compared to 2024. This was mainly
due to the below factors. As discussed above, we witnessed decline in ethanol and protein prices;
as a result, our revenue from product sales decreased by RMB15.8 million, representing a decrease
of 2.9% as compared to 2024, while our cost of sales of goods decreased by only RMB4.3 million,
representingadecreaseof0.7%ascomparedto2024.Suchdiscrepancyindecreaseofrevenuefrom
product sales and cost of sales of goods was primarily attributed to the limited reduction in cost of
sales due to fixed cost absorption and low-load production inefficiencies, and higher maintenance
and cultivation costs associated with downtime and unstable production conditions, which resulted
in a decrease in gross profit from product sales of RMB11.5 million in 2025 as compared to 2024.
Moreover, our low-carbon integrated solution projects contributed RMB22.8 million to our gross
profit in 2024, with a gross margin of 87.3%. The absence of such revenue in 2025 resulted in a
further decrease in gross profit from low-carbon integrated solutions of RMB22.8 million. Please
see “— Reasons for the Deterioration in Our Financial Performance in 2025 as Compared to 2024”
for details.

Hebei Shoulang Phase I production facility
Hebei Shoulang Phase I production facility has been in continuous operation during theTrack
Record Period, with its ethanol production of 27,326.5 tons, 27,042.7 tons and 23,750.1 tons, for
the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. The project was profitable in
2022and2023,andduringtheTrackRecordPeriod,thenetprofitandlossofHebeiShoulangPhase
I production facility amounted to a profit of RMB5.0 million, a loss of RMB23.3 million and a loss
of RMB36.6 million for the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively, mainly
due to the decreased production volume as well as the fact that ethanol price sharply declined
starting the latter half of 2024 and remained low in 2025, as detailed below.
In terms of production, the ethanol production of Hebei Shoulang Phase I production facility
remained relatively stable in 2023 and 2024. In 2025, the ethanol production decreased by
approximately 12.2% compared to that in 2024, primarily due to an increase in impurities harmful
to microbial strains in the upstream industrial off-gas in 2025, which were detrimental to the
proliferation and consumption of CO by microbial strains, resulting in increased needs to
re-inoculate the microbial strains and a further decline in production. As a result, in 2025, the
ethanol output of the Hebei Shoulang Phase I production facility decreased, and its financial
performance was adversely impacted correspondingly. Please also refer to “— Suppliers — Raw
Materials — Hebei Shoulang Phase I production facility” for more details.
In terms of the CO concentration level, the average CO concentration in the industrial off-gas
for Hebei Shoulang in the first quarter of 2026 was 46.48%, representing an increase as compared
to 45.93% in 2025 and 45.77% in 2024. This shows that the CO concentration in 2025 and the first
quarter of 2026 has recovered to a higher level.According to Frost & Sullivan, steel plants cannot
further reduce CO concentration in industrial off-gas due to production safety limits, which was in
line with our observations since 2024. We plan to enrich the carbon monoxide concentration for
Hebei Shoulang Phase I production facility after Hebei Shoulang Phase II production facility
commenced production. Please refer to “— Path to Profitability — Improve operational efficiency
by lower our production cost”.
Additionally, to address the issue of raised impurities harmful to microbial strains in the
industrial off-gas supplied to the Hebei Shoulang Phase I production facility, we have installed
additional filtration systems for such harmful impurities in the production systems of Hebei
Shoulang Phase I and Phase II production facilities, which have resolved the issue caused by such
harmful impurities. Pursuant to the industrial off-gas procurement agreement entered into between
Hebei Shoulang and its industrial off-gas supplier in 2025, there is no provision for compensation
in respect of production impact caused by an increase in such impurities in the industrial off-gas.
Accordingly, we do not currently expect to pursue a compensation claim against Hebei Shoulang’s
industrial off-gas supplier in respect of the impurity-related production impact in 2025.
In terms of pricing, the quarterly average purchase price of industrial off-gas for Hebei

of low-cost coal-based ethanol into the fuel ethanol market, fuel ethanol prices began to decline
sharply in the second half of 2024 and remained at a low level in 2025.As a result, Hebei Shoulang
PhaseIproductionfacilityexperiencedalossfortheyearendedDecember31,2024,andcombining

Shoulang Jiyuan production facility
Our Shoulang Jiyuan production facility commenced operation in March 2022. Due to the
differencesingascompositionandimpuritiesbetweentheindustrialoff-gasgeneratedbyferroalloy
mills and by steel mills, our steel plant gas purification technology was not fully compatible,
leading to unstable production and an accumulative production suspension of 52 days in the first
half of 2023. To resolve, we conducted continuous research and process optimization in 2022 and
2023, investing RMB16.7 million in technical reform, and successfully developing an effective
purification solution. Additionally, the facility also faced interruptions in the supply of industrial
off-gas due to various reasons and recorded net losses of RMB64.9 million and RMB58.6 million
for the years ended December 31, 2023 and 2024, respectively.
In 2025, the ethanol output of Shoulang Jiyuan production facility reached 21,151.74 tons,
representing an increase of 1,602.70 tons compared to that in 2024, despite the fact that the
production volume was negatively impacted by (i) the suspension of gas supply caused by the
litigationswithJiyuanJunyiwhichbeganinJune2025,and(ii)lessthanoptimallevelofgassupply
after resumption due to the ongoing litigations. Please refer to “Summary — Recent Development
and No MaterialAdverse Change — Update on Litigations with Jiyuan Junyi and Cooperation with
Jiyuan Metallurgical” for details on the litigations with Jiyuan Junyi. As to pricing, the quarterly
average selling price of ethanol remained at a low level in 2025 for Shoulang Jiyuan, mainly due
to the involution-style competition in PRC fuel ethanol market continued.As a result, in 2025, the
net loss recorded by Shoulang Jiyuan production facility increased from RMB58.6 million in 2024
to RMB82.7 million, mainly due to (i) the decrease of revenue and profit and (ii) the recognition
of a one-off impairment loss of approximately RMB22 million in the fourth quarter of 2025 due to
the uncertainties in industrial off-gas supply from its supplier.
Shoulang Jiyuan is expected to achieve a higher capacity utilization rate, benefiting from the
fact that the litigations have been fully resolved and the government-led unified gas supplier
company is expected to commence operations on or around January 2027, which, if happened, is
expectedtobenefititsprofitability.Pleasereferto“—PathtoProfitability”.AsadvisedbyourPRC
Legal Advisor, under the industrial off-gas procurement agreement, if Jiyuan Metallurgical
suspended or insufficiently supplied industrial off-gas without proper reason and caused losses to
Shoulang Jiyuan, Jiyuan Metallurgical may be liable for damages for breach of contract. However,
given that the relevant disputes with Jiyuan Junyi have been settled, and taking into account the
importance of maintaining stable cooperation with Jiyuan Metallurgical as Shoulang Jiyuan’s
existing industrial off-gas supplier, we do not currently intend to pursue further claims against
Jiyuan Metallurgical outside the settlement arrangement.
Ningxia Binze production facility
The Ningxia Binze production facility began operation in November 2022 and was in a
production ramp-up phase throughout 2023. In the first half of 2024, the Ningxia Binze production
facility experienced production suspension for 43 days due to the interruption of upstream gas
supply as a result of the market conditions in the ferroalloy industry. Consequently, Ningxia Binze
recorded a loss of RMB9.6 million and a loss of RMB76.8 million for the years ended December
31, 2023 and 2024, respectively. With the stabilization of the ferroalloy market in the second half
of 2024, the production of ethanol at Ningxia Binze production facility steadily increased to
approximately 34,476.30 tons in 2025, which was 10,717.92 tons more than the production of
23,758.38 tons in 2024, mainly because of the increase in volume of the industrial off-gas supplied
by its industrial off-gas supplier and its continuous production in 2025. However, as a result of the
low ethanol average selling price in 2025 due to similar reason with Shoulang Jiyuan, Ningxia
Binze recorded a net loss of RMB55.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, which was
narrowed as compared to that in 2024.
Ningxia Binze is expected to benefit from stabilized and further increase of the industrial
off-gas supply and, if happened, achieve a higher production outcome.After the commencement of
operation of the unified off-gas supply company, the industrial off-gas supply is expected to be
more stable and adequate to support even further increase in production, resulting in a higher
capacity utilization rate of Ningxia Binze. Please refer to “— Path to Profitability”.

Guizhou Jinze production facility
The Guizhou Jinze production facility commenced operation in June 2023 but experienced
lower-than-expected output in the first half of 2024 due to insufficient gas supply caused by
unfavorable market conditions in the ferroalloy industry. Guizhou Jinze recorded net losses of
RMB23.9 million and RMB93.8 million for the years ended December 31, 2023 and 2024,
respectively. Its industrial off-gas supplier, Yuqian Manganese, underwent equity restructuring in
the first quarter of 2025 and its gas supply was suspended during this period. Guizhou Jinze
production facility also completed its annual maintenance during the same period. Yuqian
Manganese resumed gas supply in April 2025, but normal and stable gas supply was not restored
before December 2025. Please refer to “— Supplier — Guizhou Jinze Production Facility” for
details.As a result, Guizhou Jinze production facility had a low ethanol production output in 2025.
Due to the restructuring of the industrial off-gas supplier and the high electricity price, the average
purchase price of industrial off-gas was increased in 2025, which amounted to RMB0.350 per Nm3
for each quarter, and the average selling price of ethanol remained at a low level throughout 2025,
which was RMB4,438 due to similar reasons with Shoulang Jiyuan and Ningxia Binze.As a result,
Guizhou Jinze’s net loss widened to RMB120.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2025.
After its industrial off-gas supplier restored industrial off-gas supply, Guizhou Jinze achieved a
monthly capacity utilization rate 59.60% in December 2025 and further increased to 60.3% in the
firsttwomonthsof2026.ThecapacityutilizationrateofGuizhouJinzedeclinedto43.4%inMarch
2026 due to a 10-day routine maintenance concurrently with its off-gas supplier. See “Summary —
Recent Development and No Adverse Material Change” for details.
See also “Business — Production Facilities — Existing Production Facilities” for breakeven
estimation.

According to Frost & Sullivan, the average market price of fuel ethanol in China was around
or above RMB6,000 per ton throughout 2023. In 2024, the average market price of fuel ethanol in
China declined over each quarter, mainly because the adverse effect brought by the lower priced
coal-based ethanol. In 2025, the average market price of fuel ethanol in China partially recovered
over the first three quarters due to the tightened restrictions to prevent the coal-based ethanol from
entering into the fuel ethanol market but declined again in the fourth quarter of 2025, which was
mainly due to the “involution-style” competition.The fuel ethanol price then improved again in the
first quarter of 2026, primarily because (i) from a commercial perspective, the market price
corrected following the end of the stage of “involution-style” low-price competition in the fuel
ethanol market in latter 2025, when certain market participants engaged in low-price competition
to capture market share using price below production cost. However, such irrational low-price
competitionwasnotcommerciallysustainableinthelongrun,asfuelethanolproducersstillneeded
to cover production costs and maintain continuous supply. According to Frost & Sullivan,
substantially all of the market share released as a result of the gradual exit of coal-based ethanol
had been absorbed by the fuel ethanol market by the first quarter of 2026, and “involution-style”
low-price competition had ceased in the first quarter of 2026. Government policy guidance and
industry discipline also contributed to help restore market order and curbing irrational low-price
– 154 –

=== PAGE 164 ===
BUSINESS
competition. As advised by Frost & Sullivan, when such competition eased and market order
gradually normalized in the first quarter of 2026, fuel ethanol prices rebounded in accordance with
marketdynamics;(ii)comparedwiththefourthquarterof2025,cornpricesinthemajorproduction
regionsinChinaincreasedbyRMB50toRMB100pertoninthefirstquarterof2026.Suchincrease
incornpricesincreasedcost-sidepressureoncorn-basedethanolproducers,therebyfurtherlimiting
their willingness to irrationally compete and supporting the increase in fuel ethanol prices; and (iii)
regional conflicts in the Middle East, including the Iran-related regional conflict, have affected
international crude oil prices, which indirectly contributed to the upward pricing pressure of fuel
ethanol prices in China, as advised by Frost & Sullivan.According to Frost & Sullivan, the average
Brent crude oil futures price per barrel increased 27.0% from the fourth quarter of 2025 to the first
quarter of 2026; due to the combined effect in (i) to (iii) above, during the same period, the market
price of fuel ethanol in China increased from RMB5,066.3 per ton to RMB5,370.3 per ton,
representinganincreaseofapproximately6.0%.Pleasealsosee“—PathtoProfitability”belowfor
more details on the relevant government policies.
China’s fuel ethanol supply is primarily satisfied by domestic production, with more than
99.9% of such demand satisfied by domestic supply. In 2025, China’s fuel ethanol import volume
attributed to less than 0.1% of the total fuel ethanol supply.Accordingly, China’s import volume of
fuel ethanol from major fuel ethanol producing countries such as the United States and Brazil was
extremely low, and there was little to none import of fuel ethanol from Iran. However, regional
conflictsintheMiddleEast,includingtheIran-relatedregionalconflict,haveaffectedinternational
crude oil prices, which may indirectly affect fuel ethanol prices in China. As advised by Frost &
Sullivan, although fuel ethanol prices in China are affected by multiple factors and do not move in
direct one-to-one correlation with crude oil prices, higher crude oil prices may increase the
economic attractiveness of fuel ethanol as a gasoline blending component or alternative fuel,
thereby supporting fuel ethanol demand and prices. As such, if the Iran-related regional conflict
becomes prolonged or escalates, such indirect impact may become more pronounced. In addition,
if shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is disrupted for a longer period, energy inflation may push
up costs across the fuel ethanol industry chain. For example, higher energy prices may increase
internationalfertilizerprices,whichmayinturnincreasetheproductioncostofcorn-basedethanol.
Althoughourethanolisproducedusingindustrialoff-gasratherthancorn,anincreaseinproduction
costs of corn-based ethanol may affect the overall market pricing environment for fuel ethanol in
China and in turn push the fuel ethanol prices higher. Subsequently, if any such increase in fuel
ethanol prices is reflected in our selling prices, it may have a positive impact on our revenue and
gross margin. However, geopolitical developments may also increase volatility in crude oil prices,
energy costs, logistics costs and downstream demand, which may also adversely affect our cost
structure, pricing environment, production planning and financial performance.
Our profitability during the Track Record Period was broadly correlated with the movement
in the market price of fuel ethanol in China. In general, when the market price of fuel ethanol
declined, our actual average selling price of ethanol also came under pressure, which adversely
affectedourrevenueandgrossprofit.Forexample,theaveragesellingpriceofethanolofourGroup
was RMB4,524 per ton, RMB4,763 per ton, RMB4,757 per ton and RMB4,549 per ton in each
quarter of 2025, respectively, before increasing to RMB4,696 per ton in the first quarter of 2026.
Duringthesameperiod,ourGroup’sgrosslosswasRMB21.1million,RMB21.1million,RMB37.6
millionandRMB47.7million,respectively,beforenarrowingtoRMB7.6millioninthefirstquarter
of 2026, with gross profit margin moved correspondingly. These figures illustrated that the
relatively low fuel ethanol market prices in 2025 adversely affected our profitability, while the
improvement in market prices in early 2026 contributed to the narrowing of our gross loss.
However, our profitability during the Track Record Period was also materially affected by
other factors, especially the capacity utilization rate of our production facilities, which was mainly
attributable to the stability and quality of industrial off-gas supply. In particular, lower utilisation
rates at certain production facilities in 2025 increased our unit costs and reduced our ability to
absorb maintenance and cultivation costs, thereby amplifying the adverse effect of lower ethanol
prices on our gross loss. Please also see “— Reasons for the Deterioration in Our Financial
Performance in 2025 as Compared to 2024” below for the analysis on our performance in 2025.
Accordingly, although the market price of fuel ethanol in China is an important indicator of our
pricing environment, our profitability also depended on, among others, production efficiency and
capacity utilization rate, industrial off-gas supply conditions and actual selling price based on our
sales orders.

industrial off-gas by our upstream suppliers due to repairs, equity restructuring conducted by our
upstream suppliers as well as the adverse market conditions of the PRC ferroalloy industry. Please
see the analysis below for detailed information on our production downtime.

Routine downtime
(1) Downtime due to annual routine maintenance
Ourproductionfacilitiesaredesignedtooperate8,000hoursperyear,withapproximatelyone
month reserved for annual routine maintenance, which is excluded from the 8,000 operating hours
and therefore does not affect our financial performance. During the Track Record Period, we
scheduled annual routine maintenance to align with the maintenance shutdowns of our upstream
industrialoffgassuppliers,typicallylastingaround30daysandsubjecttothescopeandcomplexity
of required tasks and any additional items identified during the process. We expect to continue
coordinating our annual maintenance with our upstream suppliers going forward.
InrespectofHebeiShoulangPhaseIproductionfacility,theroutinemaintenancedurationwas
32 days in 2023, 32 days in 2024 and 35 days in 2025. Such actual duration of maintenance is
generally consistent with the planned schedule.
TheroutinemaintenanceofShoulangJiyuanproductionfacilitytook40daysin2023,25days
in 2024 and 30 days in 2025. The extended maintenance period in 2023 was primarily because that
the absence of maintenance upon the facility’s commencement of operation in 2022 led to longer
equipment operation time and a greater number of maintenance tasks.
The routine maintenance of Ningxia Binze production facility took 23 days in 2023 and 30
days in 2024. In 2025, the facility was not scheduled for routine maintenance due to postponed
maintenance schedule as detailed in “— Our Performance during the Track Record Period —
Ningxia Binze production facility”. The duration of maintenance in 2023 and 2024 is consistent
with planned schedules.
In respect of Guizhou Jinze production facility, no routine maintenance was conducted in
2023, primarily because the facility only commenced operations in June 2023. In 2024, no routine
maintenance was scheduled because reduced industrial off gas supply meant only part of the
production lines operated at any given time, allowing maintenance to be carried out on idle lines.
The rotation between operating and non operating lines eliminated the need for overall planned
maintenance for all production lines simultaneously. The routine maintenance of Guizhou Jinze
production facility took 31 days in 2025 as planned.
Non-routine downtime
(2) Suspension of industrial off-gas supply by upstream suppliers due to sudden production
fault
The incidences of sudden production fault of industrial off-gas suppliers that caused
production suspension of two of our production facilities, excluding Hebei Shoulang Phase I
production facility and Ningxia Binze production facility which did not experience any production
suspension during the Track Record Period, are set forth below.
Shoulang Jiyuan production facility experienced four production suspensions in 2023 caused
by sudden faults at its upstream industrial off gas supplier, totaling 56 days. These included: (i) a
6 day suspension in March due to a high voltage flashover on the 35kV side leading to a power
outageforthesubmergedarcfurnace’sgasblower;(ii)a20daysuspensioninJuly-Augustresulting
from a short circuit fault in the high voltage switchgear of the supplier’s power generation
workshop; (iii) a 27 day suspension in September-October due to an internal short circuit fault in
a 220kV main transformer causing severe equipment damage; and (iv) a 3 day suspension in
Decemberfollowingthesimultaneousshutdownoftwofurnaces,whichcausedamalfunctioninthe
centrifugal compressor.
GuizhouJinzeproductionfacilityexperiencedupstreamindustrialoff-gassupplyinterruptions
totaling 62 days. These included: (i) a 12-day suspension in November-December 2023 due to low
intake pressure at the upstream ferroalloy plant’s coal-gas booster fan, triggering interlocking trips;
(ii) a 10-day suspension in June-July 2024 caused by a malfunction at the supplier’s 220kV
substation; (iii) a 4-day suspension in December 2024 resulting from a voltage dip and fault in the
supplier’s No. 2 generator unit; (iv) a 10-day suspension in June 2025 due to a sudden failure at the
upstream industrial off-gas supplier’s substation that caused a complete power outage and
shutdown; (v) a 7-day suspension in October 2025 due to an electrical failure in the control power
– 157 –

=== PAGE 167 ===
BUSINESS
supply of the upstream industrial off-gas supplier’s electric-furnace distribution room, which
caused all production equipment to lose power; (vi) a 2-day suspension in October 2025 due to a
failureofthefrequencyconverteroftheupstreamindustrialoff-gassupplier’sboosterfan;and(vii)
a 17-day suspension in November 2025 due to the upstream industrial off-gas supplier’s technical
transformation involving valve tie-ins for a newly added gas cooler.
The suspension of industrial off-gas supply had caused maintenance and cultivation costs of
RMB24.3 million, RMB5.6 million and RMB14.3 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively.
According to our estimates, had the industrial off-gas supply not been suspended due to such
reasons, we would have increased our gross profit by approximately RMB8.1 million in 2023,
reduced our gross loss by approximately RMB2.2 million in 2024 and reduced our gross loss by
approximately RMB3.7 million in 2025, respectively. If all production lines in a facility shut down
simultaneously, re-cultivating the microbial strain requires no more than 30 days, regardless of the
length of the downtime. If only part of the production lines are suspended, the re-cultivation period
is shorter than in a full-shutdown scenario.
During the Track Record Period, the upstream industrial off-gas suppliers of Hebei Shoulang
Phase I production facility and Ningxia Binze production facility never experienced any sudden
production fault. In 2023, after the sudden production fault of the industrial off-gas supplier of the
Shoulang Jiyuan production facility was repaired, there was no suspension of industrial off-gas
supply due to similar reasons in 2024. Guizhou Jinze’s upstream gas supplier has completed the
safety inspection and comprehensive maintenance of existing production facilities in the first
quarter of 2025. Based on our discussion with our industrial off-gas suppliers, their production
plans for 2026 remain stable, which is likely to lead to reliable industrial off-gas supply. Based on
the above, the management believe such production suspension is one-off event and is unlikely to
reoccur in the foreseeable future.
(3) Due to the unfavorable market conditions of the ferroalloy industry, the upstream suppliers
adjusted its production, resulting in either the suspension of or reduction in the supply of
industrial off-gas
The suspension of industrial off-gas supply had caused maintenance and cultivation costs of
RMB17.9 million in 2024. In 2024, the industrial off-gas suppliers of the Shoulang Jiyuan and
Ningxia Binze production facilities suspended production activities in response to the unfavorable
market environment, resulting in the interruption of the supply of industrial off-gas. Shoulang
Jiyuan and Ningxia Binze stopped production for 52 days and 43 days respectively. According to
our estimate, had the industrial off-gas supply not been suspended due to such reasons, we would
have reduced our gross loss by approximately RMB20.7 million in 2024.
In 2023 and 2024, the industrial off-gas supplier of the Guizhou Jinze production facility
reduced production activities due to unfavorable market conditions, and accordingly reduced the
supplyofindustrialoff-gastotheGuizhouJinzeproductionfacility.Accordingtoourestimate,had
the industrial off-gas supply not been suspended due to this reason, we would have increased our
grossprofitbyapproximatelyRMB3.5millionin2023andreducedourgrosslossbyapproximately
RMB22.0 million in 2024.
Please refer to “Industry Overview — Overview of the Steel and Ferroalloy Industry —
Analysis of China’s Steel and Ferroalloy Comprehensive Price Index” for the pricing trends of
silicomanganese in China’s ferroalloy industry for 2024 and 2025, as well as its price outlook for
2026. We expect less situations where our upstream suppliers suspend or reduce gas supply due to
the unfavorable market environment in 2026.
(4) Downtime due to technical reform
In 2023, the production facilities of Shoulang Jiyuan and Guizhou Jinze were suspended for
56 days and 20 days respectively due to technical reform. In 2024, the Shoulang Jiyuan production
facility experienced a 27-day suspension due to technical reform. Given the production issues had
been addressed, we believe that such production suspension is one-off and is unlikely to reoccur in
the foreseeable future.
The technical reform had caused maintenance and cultivation costs of RMB19.7 million and
RMB9.1millionforShoulangJiyuanandGuizhouJinzein2023,respectively.Thetechnicalreform
had caused maintenance and cultivation costs of RMB11.2 million for Shoulang Jiyuan in 2024.

BUSINESS
Had the technical reform not been implemented at the Shoulang Jiyuan and Guizhou Jinze
production facilities, we would have increased our gross profit by approximately RMB5.5 million

approximately RMB5.4 million in 2024.
In 2025 and up to the Latest Practicable Date, none of our production facilities experienced

(5) Downtime due to equity restructuring of industrial gas suppliers
The industrial off-gas supplier of Guizhou Jinze underwent an equity restructuring during the
first quarter of 2025, during which gas supply was temporarily suspended, causing Guizhou Jinze
to suspend production for 93 days. The suspension of industrial off-gas supply had caused
maintenanceandcultivationcostsofRMB23.6millionin2025.IfGuizhouJinzeproductionfacility
had not suspend production due to the equity restructuring of its industrial off-gas supplier, we
would have reduced our gross loss by approximately RMB9.2 million in 2025. Moreover, after the
completion of such equity restructuring in April 2025, the industrial off-gas supplier experienced
unstable production during its commissioning phase and conducted further technical
transformations, which further adversely impacted Guizhou Jinze’s production. Please refer to “—
Suppliers — Raw Materials — Guizhou Jinze production facility” for more details. Given that the
industrial off-gas supplier has completed its equity restructuring, we consider the production
suspension to be a one-off occurrence and unlikely to recur in the foreseeable future.
(6) Downtime due to disputes with industrial gas suppliers
The parent company of Shoulang Jiyuan’s industrial off-gas supplier engaged in a series of
litigations with us in 2025.Affected by these litigations, Shoulang Jiyuan suspended production for
22 days due to the suspension of gas supply by the industrial off-gas supplier. The suspension of
industrial off-gas supply had caused maintenance and cultivation costs of RMB3.8 million in 2025.
If Shoulang Jiyuan production facility had not suspended operations due to these litigations, we
would have reduced our gross loss by approximately RMB3.4 million in 2025. Since all litigations
between us and the industrial off-gas supplier have been withdrawn, we consider the relevant
production suspension to be a one-off incident, which is unlikely to occur again in the foreseeable
future. Please see “— Legal Proceedings and Compliance — Legal Proceedings”.

Reasons for the Deterioration in Our Financial Performance in 2025 as Compared to 2024
Our financial performance deteriorated in 2025 as compared to 2024 primarily because our
revenue decreased while our cost of sales did not decrease proportionately. Our revenue decreased
by 7.4% from RMB563.6 million in 2024 to RMB521.7 million in 2025. In contrast, our cost of
sales decreased by only RMB7.6 million, or 1.2%, from RMB657.0 million in 2024 to RMB649.4
million in 2025. As a result, our gross loss increased by RMB34.3 million from RMB93.3 million
in2024toRMB127.7millionin2025,andourgrossprofitmargindeterioratedfromnegative16.6%
to negative 24.5%. Our loss for the year widened from RMB245.6 million to RMB324.9 million.
We believe such deterioration was primarily attributable to the following factors:
(i) A decline in the average selling prices of our major products, especially ethanol.
Although our sales volume of ethanol increased from 86,868.9 tons in 2024 to 91,342.0
tons in 2025, the average selling price of ethanol decreased from RMB5,069.9 per ton
to RMB4,641.5 per ton during the same period. As a result, revenue from ethanol
decreased from RMB440.4 million in 2024 to RMB424.0 million in 2025
notwithstanding the increase in sales volume. Similarly, although our sales volume of
microbial protein increased from 10,742.6 tons in 2024 to 11,550.4 tons in 2025, the
average selling price of microbial protein decreased from RMB8,454.5 per ton to
RMB7,999.5 per ton, and the resulting increase in revenue from microbial protein from
RMB90.8 million to RMB92.4 million was not sufficient to offset the decline in ethanol
revenue.
(ii) Lower cost absorption efficiency under unstable and low-load production conditions.
During periods of unstable industrial off-gas supply or quality issues, our production
facilities were only able to operate at a low load. Although production did not always
come to a complete halt, low-load operation reduced production efficiency and cost
absorption. Fixed costs such as depreciation and labor costs, as well as certain basic
– 160 –

=== PAGE 170 ===
BUSINESS
operating costs incurred once production commences, could not be reduced
proportionately with the lower output. As a result, our cost of sales did not decrease in
line with the decrease in revenue.
(iii) Additional maintenance and cultivation costs associated with downtime. Our
maintenance and cultivation costs increased by RMB2.8 million, or 4.4%, from
RMB62.7 million in 2024 to RMB65.4 million in 2025. Such increase was mainly
attributable to non-routine downtime, fermentation halt and restart, microbial strain
re-cultivation and unstable production conditions at certain production facilities. In
particular, as further detailed below, Hebei Shoulang was affected by harmful impurities
in upstream industrial off-gas, Shoulang Jiyuan was affected by interruption and
insufficiency of industrial off-gas supply in connection with disputes and litigation
involving Jiyuan Junyi, and Guizhou Jinze was affected by the prolonged recovery of
industrial off-gas supply after its upstream supplier’s restructuring and subsequent
equipment faults and technical transformation.
(iv) Decrease in contribution from low-carbon integrated solutions. Revenue from low-
carbon integrated solutions decreased from approximately RMB26.1 million in 2024 to
nilin2025.Assuchrevenuegenerallydidnotinvolvethesameproductioncoststructure
as ethanol production, the absence of such revenue in 2025 also contributed to the
deterioration in our overall gross profit performance.
For Hebei Shoulang Phase I production facility, revenue decreased from RMB176.1 million

not optimal (45.77% in 2024 and 45.93% in 2025), while the level of harmful impurities in such
off-gas increased in 2025, adversely affecting microbial proliferation and CO-processing efficiency
and resulting in more frequent re-inoculation. The increase in harmful impurities in upstream

output and production efficiency, adversely affecting cost absorption of Hebei Shoulang and its
gross profit and gross profit margin in 2025.
For Shoulang Jiyuan production facility, ethanol capacity utilization rate increased from

Existing policies to restrict coal-based ethanol from entering the fuel ethanol market and the
introduction of additional government policies on “anti-involution” are expected to contribute to
price recovery in 2026
AccordingtoChinesegovernmentpolicy,coal-basedethanolisconsiderednon-renewableand
inconsistent with Chinese government’s policy goal of developing a sustainable fuel ethanol
industry.As a result, the PRC government has issued the following policies to limit the application
of coal-based ethanol. In October 2023, the National Energy Administration issued the Notice on
Preventing Coal-based Ethanol from Entering the Biofuel Ethanol Market and Further Regulating
the Market Order (Guo Neng Zong Tong Ke Ji [2023] No. 124) (《關於防止煤製乙醇進入生物燃
料乙醇市場進一步規範市場秩序的通知》(國能綜通科技[2023]124號)), which aimed to restrict
coal-based ethanol from entering the biofuel ethanol market and further standardize the market
systemofethanolgasoline.Anumberofprovincialandmunicipalgovernmentssubsequentlystarted
toissuedetailedrulesforregulationduringtheperiodfromthesecondhalfof2024tothebeginning
– 162 –

BUSINESS
of 2025, and carried out enforcement actions. On January 27, 2025, the General Office of the State
Council issued the Opinions on Promoting the High-quality Development of Refined Oil
Circulation (Guo Fa Ban [2025] No. 5) (《關於推動成品油流通高質量發展的意見》(國發辦
[2025]5號)), which requires the acceleration of the development of green low-carbon
transformation, promotes the upgrading of refined oil quality and the development of alternative
clean energy, and aimed to further standardize the market order of biofuel ethanol and ethanol
gasolineforvehicles.Itrequiresaseverecrack-downonillegalandirregularbehaviors.Itmandates
that local governments at all levels should coordinate the supervision and investigation of breach
of laws and regulations in the field of refined oil circulation. It strictly prohibits the sale of vehicle
fuels with gasoline or diesel as the main component and vehicle fuels which are not in compliance
with national policy regulations under the name of “new energy” or “alternative energy”. For
details, please see “Regulatory Overview — Regulations On Clean Production and Renewable
Energy — Regulatory Policies Supporting Biofuel Ethanol and Cracking down Coal-based Ethanol
Production”. In 2025, pursuant to these government policies, coal-based ethanol producers were
subjecttodisciplinarymeasuresandprohibitedfromenteringthefuelethanolmarket.Followingthe
implementation of such policies, market order initially improved as the reduction in coal-based
ethanol tightened overall market supply in the first three quarters of 2025 and the average selling
priceofethanolincreasedinthesecondandthirdquartersof2025ascomparedwiththefirstquarter
of 2025.
The exit of coal-based ethanol producers released a portion of market share, particularly
within the segment supplying to private petroleum companies where pricing is generally more
market-driven and competitive in nature, and in turn intensified competition among remaining
market participants.According to Frost & Sullivan, the “involution-style” competition observed in
China’s fuel ethanol market in the fourth quarter of 2025 primarily involved certain fuel ethanol
producers adopting below-cost pricing strategies to capture such released market share, thereby
disrupting normal market order. As further advised by Frost & Sullivan, the gradual exit of
coal-based ethanol from the fuel ethanol market released an estimated 300,000 to 500,000 tons of
marketshareperannum,representingapproximately8.3%to13.8%ofthetotalfuelethanolmarket
in China in 2025. In the fourth quarter of 2025, this development was compounded by a decline in
cornprices,whichreducedtheproductioncostsoffuelethanolproducersusingcornasrawmaterial
and enhanced their willingness and flexibility to engage in price competition. As a result,
competition for orders intensified among certain market participants in the second half of 2025.
According to Frost & Sullivan, while some lower-priced transactions emerged in October 2025, the
overall impact was relatively limited at that stage. Such “involution-style” competition intensified
in November 2025, when producers engaging in aggressive pricing accounted for approximately
20% to 25% of active market trading volume, resulting in a noticeable decline in prevailing market
pricesinNovember2025ofapproximately8%to10%ascomparedtotheaveragepricesinthethird
quarter of 2025. By December 2025, pricing gradually stabilized, and the proportion of trading
volume attributable to such aggressively pricing producers declined to below 10%. As a result,
during the fourth quarter of 2025, the market share released by coal-based ethanol producers was,
for a time, competed for through aggressive and, in certain cases, below-cost pricing strategies,
which contributed to a decrease in the price of fuel ethanol in China from RMB5,170 per ton in the
third quarter of 2025 to RMB5,066 per ton in the fourth quarter of 2025, according to Frost &
Sullivan. Over the same period, our Group’s average selling price of ethanol decreased from
RMB4,757 per ton to RMB4,549 per ton.

Improve operational efficiency by lower our production cost
Our ability to manage and control our costs of sales is critical to the success of our business
and our profitability. Our cost of sales consists of (i) cost of sales of goods and services,
representing direct costs associated with our production of goods such as ethanol and microbial
protein, provision of services, and (ii) maintenance and cultivation costs. Maintenance and
cultivation costs primarily reflect, among others, depreciation of property, plant and equipment and
utility costs that we incurred during (a) downtime due to upstream sudden production fault and
upstream market conditions, (b) downtime due to our scheduled maintenance and technical reform
and (c) the subsequent fermentation strains breeding and cultivation period.
During the Track Record Period, production suspensions or periods of low production output
and the subsequent fermentation strains breeding and cultivation period impacted our capacity
utilization rates. We had capacity utilization rates (i) for ethanol of 48.1%, 42.1% and 42.1% and
(ii) for microbial protein of 51.4%, 46.1% and 49.8% for the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024
and 2025, respectively.As a result, we had a high unit cost during theTrack Record Period and our
gross margin was 3.0%, negative 16.6% and negative 24.5%, respectively. However, as discussed
in “— Business Sustainability — Path to Profitability”, we expect the supply of industrial off-gas
will stabilize in 2026. As a result, we expect the utilization rate for our production facilities to
increase in 2026 which in turn will lead to a lower unit cost for our productions, resulting in a
substantial improvement in gross profit margin.
Wehavewitnessedsuchtrendinthefirstquarterof2026:wehadcapacityutilizationratesfor
ethanol of 54.8% for such period which was improved as compared with the average capacity
utilization rate of 42.1% in 2025. With the industrial off-gas impurity issue resolved for Hebei
Shoulang Phase I, the resolution of litigations between Shoulang Jiyuan and its upstream industrial
off-gas supplier in March 2026, the resolution of the temporary management changes related issue
by Ningxia Binze’s industrial off-gas supplier and the restoration of optimal industrial off-gas
supply for Guizhou Jinze since December 2025, we expect the average utilization rate of our
production facilities will further improve in 2026 which will lead to further reduction in unit cost
as we benefit from economies of scale. Our gross loss margin in the first quarter of 2026 improved
by approximately 19.7% as compared to the quarterly average in 2025. Please see “Summary —
Recent Development and No Material Adverse Change” for details. Moreover, as the expected
commissioning of industrial off-gas supply by government-led unified industrial off-gas supply

QUALITY CONTROL
We are committed to maintaining high standards of product quality across all our operations.
We implement strict quality control procedures throughout the entire product lifecycle, covering
procurement, production, and warehousing. Our production facilities are supported by management
systems and quality control programs. We are certified under ISO 9001 (Quality Management
System), ISO 14001 (Environmental Management System), and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health
and Safety Management System), reflecting our commitment to quality, environmental
responsibility, and workplace safety. We also have a dedicated quality control team responsible for
establishing and overseeing quality standards and inspection guidelines. To ensure the ongoing
effectiveness of our quality control system, our quality control team conducts regular internal
audits,performancereviews,statisticalanalyses,andprovidestrainingoninspectiontechniquesand
qualityawareness.DuringtheTrackRecordPeriodanduptotheLatestPracticableDate,therewere
no material incidents of failure in our quality control systems that negatively impacted our
operations.
Procurement
We have established policies and detailed procedures to ensure the quality of raw materials
purchased from our suppliers. In selecting and evaluating suppliers, we conduct thorough due
diligence, considering various factors such as product or service quality, manufacturing conditions,
and technical capabilities. We also require our suppliers to adhere to our internal supply chain
management policies. For the supply of industrial off-gas, we have specific quality control
measuresinplace.Thequalityoftheindustrialoff-gasismonitoredthroughonlineinstrumentsthat
track key indicators, such as carbon monoxide concentration and oxygen levels. If there are any
fluctuations, we will promptly communicate with the upstream suppliers to ensure the supplied
industrial off-gas meets the quality standards necessary for our production needs. Our quality
control team is responsible for ensuring compliance with these standards and conducting
inspections to confirm the industrial off-gas meets the requirements specified in our procurement
agreements.
Production
We have established a production management and quality control system to ensure that our
product quality consistently meets the required standards throughout the production process. Each
month, our production department holds production planning meetings to organize and schedule
production activities. Upon receiving sales orders, the sales team coordinates with the storage and
transportation teams to ensure that products are prepared and shipped according to established
procedures.Throughout the production process, our quality inspection department closely monitors
product quality at every stage, conducting process control tests, finished product inspections, and
final factory checks to ensure compliance with quality standards. We are also committed to
maintaining a safe and healthy working environment. In compliance with applicable requirements,
we established a safety production committee, responsible for coordinating and ensuring the
implementationoflocalsafetymanagementmeasuresacrossallbasestomaintainstableoperations.
We strictly adhere to occupational health protection requirements, providing qualified protective
equipment, conducting annual health check-ups for all employees, and enhancing employee health
monitoring.To further ensure safety, we have developed a safety management system, occupational
health management system, and safety operation procedures.We strictly comply with all applicable
laws, regulations, and national industry standards in our production and operations. During the
Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we had not encountered any material
issues related to sales returns, product recalls, or product liability claims arising from quality
control failures or safety incidents.

Warehousing
Our warehouses undergo regular inspections to ensure compliance with safety and
environmental standards. This includes the assessment of safety barriers and electrical facilities, as
wellasensuringproperventilation,dryness,cleanliness,andoverallsafetyoftheenvironment.The
warehouses are equipped with fire safety equipment, moisture control, and rodent prevention
measures to protect our inventory. In addition, the finished product tank areas are equipped with
automated control instruments, video surveillance and safety fire protection systems to enhance
security. We also conduct routine physical inventory checks to confirm the accuracy and quality of
bothauxiliarymaterialsandfinishedproducts.Thesechecksincludedailymonitoringofwarehouse
space usage to ensure it aligns with production and delivery requirements.
Transportation
We implement control measures to ensure the quality and safety of products throughout the
entire transportation process, including both raw materials and finished products. Specific quality
and safety control measures are implemented for industrial off-gas, ethanol and microbial protein
products during transportation. For industrial off-gas, the supplier is responsible for transporting it
through pipelines to our designated delivery point. The quality of the industrial off-gas is
continuously monitored through our online instruments that track carbon monoxide concentration
and oxygen levels. If fluctuations are detected, we promptly notify the supplier to make necessary
adjustments.Bothindustrialoff-gassuppliersandourCompanymustadheretosafetyprotocolsand
promptly address pipeline leakage issues. For ethanol, we offer two delivery options, namely
delivery to the locations designated by the customers or customer pick-up. In the first case, we
engage qualified third-party logistics providers to handle transportation, and the safety
responsibility during transportation lies with the third-party carrier. In the second case, customers
arrange for qualified third-party logistics providers to pick up the ethanol products from our
warehouse, and customers bear full responsibility for safety during transportation. For microbial
protein, customers are responsible for picking up the microbial protein products from our
warehouse, and customers bear the responsibility for safety during transportation.
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SYSTEMS
Our information technology systems are integrated into key aspects of our operations,
including sales management, procurement and supply chain management, production planning and
monitoring, financial and technical reporting, and human resources management. We utilize the
enterprise resource planning (ERP) system to streamline our financial management, procurement,
and sales processes. We have also implemented an office automation (“OA”) system to digitalize
our business management and internal coordination. The OA system has improved efficiency by
automating routine administrative tasks and supporting better collaboration across teams. In our
production process, we deploy a distributed control system (“DCS”) to monitor and control
operations.TheDCSsystemensuresthestabilityandefficiencyofourproductionfacilitiesthrough
continuous monitoring and performance optimization. We are also undertaking initiatives to
enhance our information technology systems, such as developing a big data platform to support
research and development in biosynthetic technologies and designing an intelligent fermentation
model for real-time adjustment of fermentation conditions during the production process. We
believe these efforts will strengthen our operational capabilities, improve efficiency, and foster
knowledge sharing across the organization.

Transition risks
In addition to the risks of natural disaster faced by physical operations, the transition to a
low-carbon society also contains hidden uncertainties, which may expose us to transition risks.The
following set forth the possible transition risks that we have identified:
Costs involved in the transition to lower emissions technology: In order to achieve cleaner
operations and production processes, we will utilize new equipments which are more energy-
efficient and environmentally friendly. This transition period involves not only a substantial
one-time capital expenditure, but also ongoing technical maintenance and a steep learning curve.
Therefore, we will adopt a phased investment strategy to test new technologies on a small scale
first, then gradually expand its application after significant results are achieved.At the same time,
by leveraging government subsidies and green financial support, and working closely with
technology providers and consulting agencies, the costs and risks in the initial stage can be
effectively managed.
Uncertaintyregardingpoliciesandregulations:Nationalandlocalgovernmentsmayintroduce
stricter environmental laws and regulations, such as higher GHG emission standards and more
stringent restrictions on intensive energy consumption.These regulations not only require us to use
cleaner and low-carbon technologies in our daily operations and production, but failure to comply
with such policies and regulations may result in significant fines or even business suspension. To
mitigatesuchrisk,wewillcloselymonitorthelatestlegaldevelopmentsregardingESGmattersand
update our ESG measures accordingly to ensure compliance with the latest relevant policies and
regulations.
Changes related to the market and supply chain: Market demand is gradually shifting towards
astrongeremphasisonlow-carbonenvironmentsandsustainabledevelopment.Theimplementation
of the carbon peak and carbon neutrality goals by the Chinese government has also accelerated the
transition of key industries, such as the industrial and energy sectors, to align with major national
development strategies. Failure to adapt to such market and supply chain-related transitions may
result in a decline in our market competitiveness and customer satisfaction, thereby impacting our
market share and profitability. To avoid such consequences, we should proactively strengthen our
relationships with supply chain partners to ensure the stable supply of raw materials, and increase
our research and development efforts in technological innovation to enhance our product
competitiveness and market adaptability.

Air emissions and GHG emissions management
Our air emissions during daily operations include nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide particulate
matter and other pollutants. The primary source of such emissions is the fermentation off-gas
produced by the fermentation unit, which is collected through pipelines, burned and processed in
the oxidation furnace, and subsequently discharged through a high chimney. Our GHG emissions
mainly stem from the off-gas treatment stage, which comprises of the carbon dioxide in the
fermentation off-gas and some carbon dioxide converted from residual carbon monoxide through
the oxidation furnace, as well as other direct and indirect GHG emissions generated from energy
consumption. We have formulated the operating procedure, the Environmental Safety Monitoring
and Measurement Control Procedure (《環境安全監視和測量控制程序》), and the third-level
documents, including the Environmental Protection Management Responsibility System (《環境保
護管理責任制》) and the Wastewater, Off-Gas and Noise Pollutant Emission Management System
(《廢水、廢氣、噪聲污染物排放管理制度》), to clarify the environmental protection
responsibilities of each department and role.
Compared to conventional uses such as industrial off-gas combustion, our existing first-
generation carbon reduction technology can achieve 33% biological carbon fixation, as calculated
and confirmed by a CCER qualified auditor. In addition, we have achieved a cumulative total of
approximately263,000tonsofethanolproduction,andreducedacumulativetotalofapproximately
1,148,000tonsofcarbonemissionsduringtheyearsfrom2023to2025,ascalculatedandconfirmed
by a CCER qualified auditor. Our synthetic biotechnology is an important initiative for
implementing the “dual carbon” target in China. In light of China’s launch of a carbon trading
market operation pilot, our main business is of great significance to the domestic industrial sector,
enablingefficientcarbonemissionsreductionatalowcostandacceleratingthetransitiontoagreen
and low-carbon economy.

According to Greenhouse Gas Protocol “Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Accounting and
Reporting Standard”, we consider the most relevant categories of Scope 3 emissions to include
purchasedgoodsandservices,wastegeneratedinoperations,businesstravel,employeecommuting,
downstream transportation and distribution, and use of sold products. Considering the data
availability and estimation uncertainty, our Scope 3 emissions estimation incorporated the key
sources of emissions from purchased goods and services (purchased chemicals and electricity used
for processing fresh water and sewage by authorities) and business travel (air travel by employees).
We recognize the growing importance of understanding and managing our broader value chain
emissions, and hence have included the Scope 3 emissions data collection procedures into our
Internal Control Assessment Report to enable the enhancement of our capability to measure and
disclose upon the Listing.
Resource consumption
The energy and resources we consume during our daily business operation are mainly
electricity and water consumption, as well as a small amount of gasoline, diesel and outsourced
heat. We have adopted energy and water resources management measures that are tailored to our
specific circumstances. We have used high-efficiency energy equipment to reduce overall energy
consumption during our technical transformation. From 2023 to 2025, we reduced the energy
consumption of our production by implementing efficiency upgrades to oxidation furnaces,
retrofitting circulating water pumps, and replacing membrane systems with fermentation
centrifuges. Furthermore, all of our production facilities reuse part of the residual distillate water
from the clear liquid of the distillation system in the fermentation system, reducing the process
water consumption of the fermentation system by 50%.
As part of our commitment to sustainable development, we have set ESG targets and will
deploy relevant resources to achieve them. Our goal is to reduce the environmental impacts of our
businessoperationswhileloweringlong-termoperatingcosts.BelowsetsforthourESGtargetsand
the associated plans and measures.
 Intensity of comprehensive energy consumption: By 2028, we aim to reduce the
intensity of comprehensive energy consumption by 10% compared to 2024.
In 2025, we conducted an energy audit of our production facilities to identify areas for
energy optimization and transformation. Based on the findings, we replaced
conventional lighting with high brightness and low-energy-consuming LEDs, added
automated adjustment settings to the lighting system to automatically adjust the lights
according to seasonal and time-based changes, and initiated and promoted the “Energy
Saving Week” event to engage employees in energy-saving efforts. At the same time,
Guizhou Jinze also carried out renovations on the aeration pipes in the oxygen tanks,
reducing the operating energy consumption of the aeration blowers by more than 20%.

Waste and wastewater management
The hazardous wastes generated during our ordinary course of business includes waste
activated carbon, waste engine oil, waste reagents and waste catalysts, and the general solid wastes
include sludge generated from the wastewater treatment system.All types of hazardous wastes are
stored in a hazardous wastes temporary storage room after generation and are regularly transferred
to qualified facilities for treatment. The sludge produced from the wastewater treatment system is
treated centrally by the solid waste treatment plant after dehydration, or sold for comprehensive
utilization.
The wastewater generated in our ordinary course of business mainly refers to the clear liquid
wastewater generated after the centrifugation of the concentrated fermenting mash containing
microbial protein. We have incorporated the wastewater treatment process into the regular
production process. After treatment, part of the wastewater is reused in the fermentation process;
another portion is utilized for replenishing the circulating cooling water, and the rest is discharged
after reaching the required standards.
